attacks.claim: Share links embed the owner's live project API key in the URL query string (`k`), and the share page returns it to any viewer as `replayKey`. Anyone with the link, including Slack/X unfurl crawlers, browser history, referrers and logs, obtains a credential that can spend the owner's paid (pro) quota.
attacks.evidence: url.searchParams.set("k", project.apiKey); ... return { messages: share.messages, model: share.model, replayKey: url.searchParams.get("k") };

attacks.claim: Deleting a share only removes the share row (404); the embedded key is the project's real credential and stays valid. Links already distributed, cached or unfurled remain exploitable until the owner manually rotates the key. QA only checked the 404, not key invalidation.
attacks.evidence: Shares can be deleted from Playground → History; deleted shares return 404. / Share link: create, open in incognito, re-run, delete → 404: pass.

attacks.claim: Anonymous replay is billed to the owner's project quota with no per-link limit, expiry or abuse control. Pro is billed per token with daily_tokens null, so a viral link driven by the HN/X launch is an open spending endpoint. Release notes do not disclose this exposure.
attacks.evidence: // Viewers without an account replay against the owner's project quota.

attacks.claim: Deployed free-tier rate limit is 20 requests per second (burst 40), but the public changelog promises 20 per minute. This is a 60x difference. QA passed only against a staging config using `per: minute`, so the prod config was never tested.
attacks.evidence: rate_limit: { requests: 20, per: second, burst: 40 } vs "20 requests per minute"; "(staging config used `per: minute`)"

attacks.claim: The advertised 100k tokens/day free quota has no corresponding `daily_tokens` setting in the free tier config, so it may not be enforced. With email-only signup, no card and no verification, multi-account abuse is easy.
attacks.evidence: free: { models, rate_limit, max_tokens_per_request: 4096, pool: free-8b } (no daily_tokens) vs "100k tokens per day"

attacks.claim: The $4k hard budget is not enforced. The $3.6k estimate assumes 2 replicas at the projected load, but the pool autoscales to 24 H100s (~$1.4k/day) on queue depth with a 20 rps limit. There is no spend cap or kill switch, and alerts fire only on replicas > 6 and error rate, not on spend or token burn. Launch-spike traffic and an unmeasured 30% utilization figure with no load test make overrun likely.
attacks.evidence: max_replicas: 24 ... Alerting: free pool replicas > 6 pages on-call; error rate > 2% pages on-call.

attacks.claim: Rollback only stops new signups. Existing free keys keep consuming GPUs, and share-link creation/replay (and /v1/usage) ship unflagged at 16:00 with no independent off switch, so the key leak and public replay persist after rollback.
attacks.evidence: Rollback: `free_signup_open` off stops new signups; existing free keys keep working.

attacks.claim: Full conversation contents are copied into public, server-rendered, unfurlable share pages with no stated retention, noindex, or user-facing warning about what is exposed (including the key and any pasted secrets or personal data). Deletion says nothing about cached or unfurled copies.
attacks.evidence: messages: session.messages ... Share pages are server-rendered with Open Graph tags so links unfurl nicely on Slack/X.
